analysis.title: 'Le Pause': Stocks Hit Record Highs As Marine Calms Markets After The Storm...
key_insights: SPX and NDX closed at record highs on Oct 6 while RTY lagged. A fiscally responsible budget from Marine Le Pen narrowed the OAT/Bund spread by 30bps, lowered bond yields and the dollar, and lifted stocks. The election is still far off and nothing is set.
The rally was driven by an Alphabet and Constellation Energy energy deal tied to the AI CapEx spend narrative. AI outperformed ex-AI, and NeoClouds, optical networking and data centers outperformed.
Semis and memory lagged, with STX -8.75% and WDC -6.5% on competition concerns tied to Toshiba.

Oil fell early on logistics, not peace, then rebounded to unchanged on attacks and explosions. Hormuz crude flows are reportedly near 76% of prewar levels and the G7 is releasing emergency stockpiles. The diesel shortage persists as Ukraine and Russia trade drone attacks on refineries.

The Vitol CEO estimates about 12 million b/d of crude and 2 million of products recently exited the strait, near the 10-14 million b/d of crude needed to balance the market into winter. Western inventories are effectively exhausted. The planned G7 release of up to 100 million barrels is a bridge, not new structural supply.
Heating-oil and gasoil cracks are near recent highs. Brent backwardation is high, though implied volatility and call skew have eased.

UST yields fell and ignored the afternoon rebound in crude. Rate-hike odds were flat. Treasury Secretary Bessent said growth and spending restraint will 'very quickly' alter the path of government borrowing. Macquarie's Gareth Berry is skeptical because the deficit is 6% and there is no plan to reduce it.
Bond volatility remains higher than equity volatility. The new SPX high came with more new lows than new highs, and NDX is breaking out relative to RTY after a roughly two-year sideways range.
Momentum traded lower again after a sharp September rebound. Goldman's high-beta momentum long basket underperformed and the short side squeezed higher.
SpotGamma shows SPX gamma getting thick above 7,800, implying a slower rate of upside change. Resistance is at 7,820 then 7,850, and support is at 7,800 and 7,775. VIX briefly hit a 14 handle.

Goldman's trading desk saw activity at 4 out of 10 and flow about 7% better to buy. Long-only funds are better buyers in info tech, financials and healthcare. Hedge funds are 14% better buyers in financials, healthcare, info tech and communication services.

BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky says breakouts to new highs are generally not something to fade, but breadth, rates and credit cross-currents suggest this breakout may not do as well as expected. The Aug 4 breakout lasted 2 days before SPX went sideways for two months.

Goldman's Brian Garrett notes US L/S net leverage is at its lowest since April 2025 and near five-year lows in the 2nd percentile. Further index gains could force investors to chase, producing 'spot up, vol up' days given low vols.
Hyperscaler stocks surged back to 4-month highs while hyperscaler credit did not follow. The dollar dipped as EUR rallied, gold rose and bitcoin ended unchanged after failing to rally.

geopolitical: France: Marine Le Pen's shadow budget calmed EU angst, narrowed OAT/Bund spreads, and was called France's 'Liz Truss moment'. The election is a long way off.
Iran: no direct US-Iran confrontation since the UN General Assembly. Iranian tanker attacks threaten the export rebound, with explosions heard from the sea at the Qeshm Island facility.
Ukraine and Russia are trading drone attacks on refineries and infrastructure, sustaining the diesel shortage. Moscow is exporting more crude while restricting diesel sales.
US midterms: the Alphabet deal made investors forget about the midterms and the risk of a Democratic win.

tension_points.bull_case: Breakouts to new highs are generally not something to fade (BTIG's Krinsky). Low L/S net leverage in the 2nd percentile could force investors to chase the index higher.
tension_points.bear_case: Breadth, rates and credit cross-currents suggest the breakout may not hold. New lows exceeded new highs, hyperscaler credit did not follow equities, and the Aug 4 breakout lasted only 2 days.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Macron rejecting Le Pen's budget plan, which would reverse the French fiscal relief.

tension_points.bull_case: Bessent says growth and spending restraint will 'very quickly' alter the path of US borrowing and 'bend that curve'.
tension_points.bear_case: Macquarie's Berry says a 6% deficit with no plan to reduce it means a stated ambition is not a plan, and investors were reluctant to call an end to the bond selloff.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A meaningful decline in energy prices, crude and refined products, which is the number one condition for a rally across the curve.
